newsitem.title: USA: KCS Q3 net off on natgas marketing loss.
newsitem.headline: KCS Q3 net off on natgas marketing loss.

text.p: KCS Energy Inc Tuesday reported a lower third quarter profits citing limits on its Woyming production and a natural gas marketing loss.

The $20.1 million in third quarter EBITDA -- earnings before depletion, depreciation, amortization, interest expense, interest and other income and income taxes -- "pushed our nine-month EBITDA total to a record $66.1 million, up 20 percent compared to EBITDA of $55.2 million for the same period last year."

Lower gas production under KCS' above-market, take-or-pay contract with Tenneco Inc, higher interest costs and a higher effective tax rate offset the benefits of higher overall oil and gas production and higher average spot market oil and natural gas prices during the nine-month period, the company said.
This resulted in a 3.0 percent decline in earnings to $4.0 million, or $0.33 per share, for the quarter and a 5.6 percent decline to $14.8 million, or $1.25 per share, for the nine-month period.

"The third quarter was also negatively impacted by our natural gas marketing operations, which had earned a small profit during the first half of the year," KCS said. "In the third quarter, this segment of our business recorded a $1.4 million loss compared to a $1.9 million loss in the same period last year, on substantially lower volume and revenue.
"While historically the third quarter has been the weakest for the gas marketing industry as well as our own operations in terms of profitability, such losses are unacceptable."
KCS said it is moving to reduce operating costs and concentrate on the marketing of its own production.

"Although oil and gas production and EBITDA were up significantly from last year, production for the quarter was relatively flat compared to the second quarter, principally due to continued limitations on the amount of sour gas we can flare and therefore on the amount of our oil production in the Manderson Field in Wyoming.
"We expect to have those constraints eased during the fourth quarter, when our injection and treatment facilities begin operations."

Noting it has drilled and completed 18 Manderson Field wells and recompleted one existing well since its discovery of the field in the Big Horn Basin of north central Wyoming, KCS said it is completing four wells and drilling 2 wells in the Phosphoria Dolomite formation in the field.

It said the completed wells, in which the company owns a 100 percent working interest, have tested at rates ranging from 200 to 1,900 barrels of oil and from 450,000 to 4.0 million cubic feet of sour natural gas per day.
Daily production is currently constrained to about 1,500 barrels of oil and 2.0 million cubic feet of natural gas due to limitations by on the amount of sour gas that can be flared.
"The key to realizing the potential of the Manderson Field is the proper handling of sour gas production," KCS said.

"We currently expect to have our injection system begin operations in November and our amine treatment plant in late December," the company said. Combined, these facilities will provide capacity for handling up to 16 millio cubic feet of sour natural gas per day and for production of some 10,000 barrels of oil per day.
It noted about half of the natural gas will be treated for sale and half reinjected for pressure maintenance.
